articles.title: Kylie Cantrall Surprises Fans With Private Acoustic Set in Downtown L.A.
articles.summary: The actress-singer, who broke out with her role as Red in Disney's 'Descendants' movies, took over Moxy Downtown Los Angeles to perform for fans on Tuesday night.
articles.content:
On the heels of her Valley Girl Problems Tour, Kylie Cantrall played a surprise intimate acoustic set in downtown Los Angeles on Tuesday night for a crowd of enthusiastic fans who sang along with all of her tunes.

Cantrall took over Moxy Downtown Los Angeles for the special event, which also celebrated her EP, Valley Girl Problems, which debuted in July. The event was part of Moxy Hotels’ ongoing music series, which brings emerging and buzzy artists together with fans for intimate experiences at Moxy properties around the world (other recent events have featured Ayra Starr in the U.K.). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Mumford & Sons' Ben Lovett to Open New Venue At Brooklyn's Domino Sugar Refinery Lifestyle Kel Mitchell Bringing 'Kel's Burger Fest' to Los Angeles: "It's a Full-On Burger Bonanza"

The actor-singer — who has starred in two of Disney's Descendants movies, playing Red, daughter of the Queen of Hearts — noted onstage that Los Angeles was her hometown and she was "feeling the love" at Moxy DTLA that night.

After asking how many people were also at her recent tour — many in the audience were — she shared: "That show was a mix of emotions. I was so sad," she said, and then a fan said she had cried during the show. "I made you cry? That should be a disclaimer on my website: If you're coming to a Kylie show, there's a chance you're going to cry. But you're going to shake a little ass too," she quipped. "It's a mix of both. That's me in a nutshell honestly — crying and shaking ass at the same time."

Cantrall said she was missing being on tour when Moxy Hotels reached out about the surprise pop-up L.A. show, and she said jumped at the chance to perform in the intimate venue. Addressing the fans, she continued, "Thank you guys for coming at the last minute." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She performed four songs at the event, kicking off with "Carrie Bradshaw," a tribute to Cantrall's "favorite TV character," the one played by Sarah Jessica Parker in Sex and the City. "She's is a fashion icon; she's kind of a mess as well, but we love her for it," Cantrall said. (The bar at Moxy DTLA was serving special cocktails in honor of the event that included the Carrie Cosmo and the Valley Girl Martini.)

Next up was "Oversized," from her previous EP, B.O.Y. (Deluxe). She revealed that she's a "hoodie stealer," joking that she had about five of her best friend's hoodies at her house. In co-writing the song, "I was kind of inspired by this era I was in, dating and dealing with guys with hoodies. … I definitely still have two of (my ex's) hoodies that I never gave back, but he never asked for them back. And they look better on me anyway," she joked.

"You know we're gonna get in our feels for a minute," she said, introducing the next song, the emotional "Space Between" from Valley Girl Problems. "Now that I've been home, I've been writing the next album … but I haven't written any ballads on it so far. That just goes to show you we're healed. We're healing slowly day by day. This song is very special to me. If you're going through something right now, or maybe you're healing through a situation, maybe even this song helped you heal a little bit." After, a fan told her that song always makes her cry, to which Cantrall responded that it makes her emotional as well. She also gave the crowd a note of encouragement: "You are so entitled to feeling whatever you're feeling … and I think the best thing we can do as humans is just try to embrace our imperfections and let that shit go, whether it's writing it down, talking to someone, therapy, writing music, creating art. … You are never alone." (Here she quipped that it was her first 18-and-older show, so she didn't have to censor herself as when she was on tour.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Cantrall closed the show with "Elastic," which she said was so frequently requested during her tour that she wound up adding it to her setlist. She wrapped with an a capella sing-along to a few verses of "Valley Girl Problems" to the delight of those inside Moxy DTLA.

Indeed, many of those in attendance sang along with her songs throughout the performance, and Cantrall engaged in some fun banter with the fans. Afterward, she asked the crowd to take a group photo before graciously signing autographs and taking selfies with fans' phones.

Cantrall recently hit 15 cities across North America as part of her first-ever headlining tour, which kicked off Sept. 25 in Minneapolis and wrapped up Oct. 22 in Los Angeles, her hometown. Next, she's set to appear on three dates of the Jingle Ball tour (Dec. 1 in Dallas, Dec. 14 in Washington, D.C. and Dec. 15 in Philadelphia). In summer 2025, she toured North America as part of Disney's Descendants/Zombies: Worlds Collide Tour.

Valley Girl Problems, released via Republic Records, follows on the heels of her debut EP, B.O.Y. The new nine-track EP was produced by Grammy-winning hitmaker Tricky Stewart (Rihanna, Tyla) and written alongside acclaimed songwriter Tayla Parx.

Moxy Hotels says that its music series aims to create a space where Gen Z can be connected with artists, events and moments shaping culture.

articles.title: The Best Gifts for Musicians and Music Fans in 2026: Fender Guitars, DJ Decks, Vinyl Sets and More
articles.summary: Everyone has a music lover in their life, and the holidays are the perfect time to get them something special, whether it’s a record player, a CD box set, a nice pair of headphones or some earplugs to protect their hearing at concerts. articles.content:
Everyone has a music lover in their life, and the holidays are the perfect time to get them something special, whether it’s a record player, a CD box set, a nice pair of headphones or some earplugs to protect their hearing at concerts.

Variety has curated this list of the best music books, home stereo systems and personal listening devices — as well as instruments and gear for both beginners and veteran musicians — so you can surprise your audiophile friend or guitar-playing relative with the perfect present this holiday season. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Noel Clarke Trial Set for 2027 Over Alleged Sex Offenses ‘Ginny & Georgia’ Sets Season 4 Release Date, Drops First Look Photos

While Squier is Fender’s entry-level guitar line, it feels slightly unfair to call one a “beginner guitar” considering its quality. In the Squier Classic Vibe Series, Fender has expanded its collection of vintage-inspired designs at an affordable price, with Stratocasters, Jaguars and two limited-edition Telecasters . The guitars come in all sorts of colors, from Fiesta Red to White Blonde to Lake Placid Blue. This guitar is the perfect gift for a new shredder who is serious about upping their game.

For the serious musician, touring guitarist or passionate hobbyist looking for a more substantial product, the Fender New American Professional is a sleek, sexy and strong piece of hardware. The Telecasters have a comfortable, flexible bridge and single-coil pickups that deliver the snappy twang synonymous with the brand. Plus, it comes with a Deluxe Molded hardshell case for taking music on the go.

For musicians who wish to record music on the go, the Fender AudioBox Go is a basic interface that lets you plug in and set up anywhere. It may not be as dynamic as higher-tech options, like the classic Focusrite Scarlett 2i2, but it’s more compact and — at its low price point — offers everything a beginner will need for laying down audio tracks. Each purchase also comes with a six-month Fender Studio Pro trial.

Be the life of the party with the Akai Numark Party Mix III, a Bluetooth DJ controller with stems control and a beat-synced LED light show. Beginner DJs can learn how to mix tracks and pump up the jams from their phone or tablet.

Chances are you’ve heard a Shure SM7 without knowing it: on the radio or even on your favorite podcast. It’s the industry standard mic that makes voices sound rich, warm and close. The SM7dB is the newest and most headache-free version. Its built-in booster makes it sound great plugged into a simple home setup, and a couple of switches let you fine-tune the tone. For the friend starting a podcast or recording the next great American album, this mic is an upgrade they’ll hear instantly.

A simple sound bar can work wonders on a home television setup. Yamaha’s brand new B200A, perfect for sound enhancement in TV, gaming and music streaming, features a built-in subwoofer and Dolby Atmos. You’ll never complain again about not being able to hear the dialogue in your favorite show. Check out Variety’s home theater awards with more soundbar and audio options here .

For those looking to further optimize the sound in their living rooms or home theaters, Yamaha’s RX300A AV receiver is an intuitive system that serves as a flexible hub for all sorts of speaker layouts. With an easy setup, you can tailor immersive audio to any space at home.

A wireless smart speaker with built-in Dolby Atmos, the Denon Home 600 is a powerful, standalone stereo device for the home. It’s for casual music listeners and audiophiles looking for one speaker with built-in subwoofers and an eight-driver array creating a three-dimensional, immersive sound. If this price point is too high, Denon also makes two smaller models, the 200 and the 400.

Turn your living room into a full-fledged home theater with Sony’s Bravia Theater Trio, all you need to create a simple surround-sound experience at home. The three-speaker design works best with large televisions, and the product was created in collaboration with Sony Pictures Entertainment so the sound lives up to the blockbuster standard of today’s filmmakers. With the Bravia Connect app, the system can be calibrated and controlled from your smartphone.

For the new guitar player who hasn’t quite found their desired feel, this Tortex Variety Pack comes with 12 picks across six different gauges. The matte surface makes them easy to grip, and the bright colors will make any guitarist stand out.

As far as high-end headphones go, the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 are top of the line. They’re sleek and comfortable, and the sound quality is excellent. These premium headphones are made in four color options, and they come with a flat, zipper case for portability. With excellent noise cancellation, the Px8 S2s are perfect for flying.

For the person in your life who has been collecting records for years but still sticks to streaming, this fully automatic, analog turntable from Denon is a great introduction to playing vinyl. It has an easy, two-button setup and premium sound quality. And it features a built-in phono pre-amp, meaning it can plug directly into speakers or a stereo without extra gear. Check out more of the best record players to shop this year here .

These Pioneer speakers can help upgrade your DJ setup or even just your home office. These compact 4-inch monitors can pair over Bluetooth for everyday listening, or plug into a mixer when it’s time to light up the party. Sleek enough for a dorm or living room, and available in white too, the DM-40D-BTs are a gift that gets cranked up the day they’re unwrapped.

Do you know someone who can’t stop talking about their guitar? Or someone who can’t seem to ever find their keys? Well, if those happen to be the same person, the Fender Jack Rack is the perfect household accessory. The wall-mounted key holder is a pint-sized replica of a classic Fender amp — it looks and feels exactly like one, with four input jacks across the front. And it comes with four quarter-inch-cable keychains, so you can plug in every time you get home.

The only downside to being a concert junkie is the morning-after ring. Most music fans don’t want to dilute the sound of live music with crappy foam earplugs, and custom plugs can be quite expensive. The Loop Experience 2 earplugs have an acoustic channel and mesh filter that turn the volume down by 17 dB while keeping the music clear. Plus, they’re shaped like jewelry and come in a variety of colors. For those with a front-row habit who are conscious about their hearing, the Loops are a perfect and affordable gift.

Long before you could play a synth on your smartphone, there was the Stylophone: a palm-sized instrument you play by touching a brass-tipped stylus to a metal keyboard. Invented in 1967, it buzzed its way onto David Bowie’s “Space Oddity,” Kraftwerk’s “Pocket Calculator” and the White Stripes’ “Icky Thump.” This affordable reissue is faithful to the original instrument’s charming tone and offers a vibrato function. Anyone can find a melody in minutes, which makes it a perfect gift for seasoned musicians and total beginners alike.

A must-read classic for anyone interested in punk or rock — or a loved one who recently moved to New York — “Just Kids” chronicles Patti Smith’s young adulthood in Manhattan, when she met and fell in love with the artist Robert Mapplethorpe. It’s a music memoir, yes, but it’s more than that. Smith’s impeccable prose teems with possibility as she writes of friendship, music and growing up. It won the National Book Award in 2010. Check out more celebrity memoirs to shop here.

Often considered one of the best rock books ever written, “Trouble Boys” tells the exciting but often heartbreaking story of the Replacements, a band that should have been huge but did everything possible to make sure they weren’t. With access to its surviving members, author Bob Mehr wrote about the foundational alternative rock band behind “Can’t Hardly Wait” and “I Will Dare.” Behind the music, it’s a gripping story about brotherhood and self-sabotage.

In “Dilla Time: The Life and Afterlife of J Dilla, the Hip-Hop Producer Who Reinvented Rhythm,” Dan Charnas tells the story of the Detroit producer who changed hip-hop and died tragically at 32. This biography explains how J Dilla revolutionized rhythm itself and became one of the most influential beat makers of all time, a music titan who continues to loom large over his genre.

Bob Dylan’s Rolling Thunder Revue is one of the most famous tours in music history. Now you can listen to the live recordings from the second leg with this sprawling box set. Spread across 39 CDs are 22 performances from spring 1976, with 371 of its 381 tracks never before released. Dylan sounds explosive and raw, furnishing his most iconic songs with a full band including Mick Ronson, Scarlet Rivera and T Bone Burnett, with Joan Baez dropping in for duets. Shop more new vinyl releases here.

For the Tom Petty fanatic in your life, the “Origins” box set covers the rocker’s early years in the 1970s, when he and the Heartbreakers churned out some of the best rock songs of all time, like “American Girl” and “Breakdown.” The four-CD set includes 50th-anniversary editions of the band’s first two albums and a blistering 1977 set from the Record Plant, as well as a DVD of their 1978 Old Grey Whistle Test appearance, a Blu-ray of Atmos mixes and a 46-page fanzine.

articles.title: Netflix to Adapt ‘Grendel’ Comic Books Into Adult Animated TV Series
articles.summary: 'Widow’s Bay' producer Bobak Esfarjani will showrun, write and executive produce the series based on Matt Wagner’s dark vigilante creation.
articles.content:
The long-running comic book series Grendel is getting a TV series adaptation from Netflix .

The streamer announced the upcoming adult animation series on Wednesday as it revealed Widow’s Bay producer Bobak Esfarjani will showrun, write and executive produce.

Grendel , created by veteran comics artist and writer Matt Wagner, follows the author Hunter Rose, whose world is turned upside down after the murder of the woman he loves. But as he becomes the revenge-obsessed vigilante Grendel, he faces the choice of whether to return to a more normal life or become something closer to a villain than a hero. While Comico debuted the series in 1982, Dark Horse Comics has recently published the title. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Beyond the Book From Book Club to Netflix: How Katherine Center's 'The Bodyguard' Became 'Guarding Stars' Movies Lee Chang-dong on the Mysteries and Meaning of 'Possible Love'

Bobak, Dark Horse Entertainment and Bobbypills are bold storytellers who love this world as much as its fans do, and we’re so excited to partner with them to bring this story to screen.”

The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures has announced its winter film series and education programs, which include “ Sing Sing ” (2024), “Blue Sky” (1994) and “Cabin Fever” (2002) among the highlights.

The season includes the museum’s annual 3D-cember series and Present Past, its celebration of film preservation. Present Past will premiere a 4K restoration of William Wyler’s “Wuthering Heights” (1939). Filmmaker and actor Carlos López Estrada (“Blindspotting,” “Raya and the Last Dragon”) will lead a Finding Your Story Workshop. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Berlin Prizewinner 'Chronicles From the Siege' Pulled From Marrakech Festival by Algerian Producer Over Morocco-Israel Ties 'Top Boy' Star Hope Ikpoku Jr. to Lead British Urban Gothic Horror 'One Night' Alongside Ellie Mejia (EXCLUSIVE)

Two-time Oscar nominee Colman Domingo will appear at a screening of “Sing Sing” (2024), presented with the museum’s Teen Council. Domingo was nominated for best actor for his role as John “Divine G” Whitfield, a man incarcerated at Sing Sing Correctional Facility who finds purpose in the prison’s theater program.

“One of the most rewarding things about being an actor is having the opportunity to bring stories and people to the screen that audiences might not be familiar with,” Domingo said. “I am thrilled to revisit ‘Sing Sing’ and share this story at the Academy Museum with the Teen Council and continue the conversations that a film like this can inspire.”

articles.title: Newsmax Sues to Block Fox-Roku Deal
articles.summary: The right-wing cable channel pointed to the allegedly unusual way in which the Justice Department approved the deal, which catapults Fox into a major player in media and streaming.
articles.content:
Newsmax, the conservative cable news channel, has filed a lawsuit challenging Fox Corp.’s $22 billion acquisition of Roku , alleging the deal will undermine competition in free ad-supported streaming.

In a lawsuit filed on Wednesday in California federal court, Newsmax argues the merger will give Fox more than 70% of the market in violation antitrust laws. It targets the Justice Department's clearance of the acquisition with minimal concessions.

"DOJ virtually never clears a transaction combining the two leading competitors in a concentrated market; it typically demands divestiture of one or the other to protect competition," states the complaint. "In this case, however, DOJ allowed this merger to an effective monopoly to close unchallenged." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Fox Agrees to Keep Roku Open to Rivals in Justice Department Greenlight Business Charlie Collier and Anjali Sud Exit Fox as New Digital Structure Set at Company

Fox closed the deal earlier this month, ahead of the 2027 target date identified by Fox executives. Hours after the announcement, the Justice Department issued a press release stating that it wouldn't sue to block the merger. It said that it concluded the deal is “not likely to result in harm to competition” in free ad-supported streaming.

Under the agreement with competition regulators, Fox will remain open to rivals. The company will continue carrying non-Fox movies and TV shows for at least three years, ensure competing services aren’t pushed down in search results or denied prominent placement on home screens and make audience data available to third parties. It also agreed to maintain safeguards preventing it from sharing sensitive information about rival content providers, including data on what users search for, watch and click until at least 2029. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Newsmax, which leans on The Roku Channel for the distribution of its news channel, reached out to Fox over concerns that the commitments obtained by the government had no mechanism ensuring compliance, according to the complaint. Fox was asked to sign an agreement making them enforceable, the lawsuit says, which was rejected.

"Far from alleviating the competitive concerns raised by the merger to monopoly between Fox and Roku, DOJ’s unusual press release – and Fox’s failure to stand by the commitments in that press release – underscores the need for judicial intervention," writes David Schwarz, a lawyer for Newsmax, in the filing.

The Justice Department typically negotiates consent decrees when it finds that a transaction will likely harm competition without concessions. The agreement is then released to the public and reviewed by the court, which ensures compliance with the merging companies' obligations. In this case, the government didn't appear to identify such a settlement.

In the lawsuit, Newsmax says the merger will substantially harm competition. The Roku Channel accounts for roughly 42% of all viewing time on free ad-supported services, with Tubi accounting for over 28%, according to Nielsen data. The 71% market share owned by the combined company should be presumptively anticompetitive under antitrust laws, the lawsuit claims.

The deal creates a new power player in media and streaming. Fox now owns two of the largest free streaming video platforms in Tubi and Roku, plus a premium streaming service in Fox One. And through Roku, it gains control of a behemoth distribution platform through which millions of households access TV, including applications operated by competitors like Netflix, YouTube and Disney+. Roku’s operating system powers its own streaming devices and is built into TVs. Its home screen is the gateway to those services for a significant chunk of the United States: Viewers use it to find apps, search for programming and, perhaps most important, decide what to watch. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Fox will have the ability to handicap rivals by giving its own services premium home-screen placement, steering viewers to its properties when they search for content and deprioritizing competitors in recommendation features, according to the complaint.

The megamerger had been more than a year in the making, though it closed in just five months.

articles.title: Angry Caregivers Are Using SNL’s Sister To Call Out Family Members On Social Media
articles.summary: One of the best SNL sketches in years is producing some strong reactions.
articles.content:
The goal of sharing a Saturday Night Live sketch is typically to elicit a laugh, but now and again, one makes such a thoughtful or important point that people use it as a conversation starter or as evidence to prove a point. That’s exactly what’s going on with last weekend’s Sister sketch , a fake commercial about how caregiving responsibilities overwhelmingly fall on the women in the family. Tens of thousands have taken to social media to share or retweet the sketch alongside comments about how they feel seen, and now, we’ve reached the point where people are using it to call out their own family members.

Actually, I probably phrased that second one too nicely. What many people are doing is throwing up their middle fingers at family members and telling stories about their avoidance and/ or woeful incompetence. Here’s a story with more than 69,000 likes …

That wild story is definitely not an outlier either. The angry rants are just pouring out of people, an overwhelming majority of whom are women who feel like they are left doing everything while their siblings live their lives. Some are mad about how they did everything until their parent died, only to find out their absentee sibling(s) got the exact same inheritance. Others are mad about how their family members infrequently show up and then critique the job they were doing and question the decisions they make.

Seriously, don’t take my word for it. Look wherever the Sister sketch is embedded. You’ll immediately start running into story after story of angry people who need to let it out. I saw one woman calling out the parent they’re looking after for raising her brother to think he didn’t need to help. I’ve seen numerous lawyers , nurses , dementia care workers and doctors saying they see the same dynamic over and over again. I saw one woman say her brother who lives near her mom can’t be bothered to help; so, she has to travel across the country to handle things.

It’s clear this sketch, which is filled with fun little easter eggs , struck a nerve, but it seems like in a very therapeutic way. It’s allowing people to give voice to frustrations they’ve clearly had for a long time, and if it leads to even some family members doing a little self-reflecting and helping out a bit more, it’ll be a huge victory. You can watch the sketch in full below...

Saturday Night Live is off for a few weeks for the holidays, but it’ll return in early December with the next new episode guest hosted by Amanda Seyfried . Fingers crossed she’s able to give us something that makes even a fraction of the cultural footprint. You can catch previously aired episodes streaming with a Peacock subscription .

articles.title: I Found Out Who Voiced Obsession’s One Wish Willow Guy (And Other Cool BTS Details)
articles.summary: I can't get enough of this movie.
articles.content:
Obsession is that one film on the 2026 movie schedule that we can’t stop talking about, and why would we want to? Now we can stream it to our heart's content with a Netflix subscription , I needed to dig up all the fun behind-the-scenes facts I learned from writer/director Curry Barker. Each of these made me think of the movie in a whole different way! Let’s get into it. (SPOILERS ahead.)

I’m always curious about how movies change over time, and Barker told CinemaBlend about one pivotal scene that he played around with a lot. The writer/director was also the movie’s editor on the $750k independent production, and he told us about one exchange he tried a bunch of different ways . In his words:

This sort of blew my mind because this is the scene I was playing over and over in my head after seeing the movie. It’s an important scene because it establishes Bear and Nikki’s relationship before Nikki loses her autonomy. Watching that scene made me wonder if Bear could have had a shot with Nikki if he had simply asked her out rather than using the One Wish Willow. With that in mind, I totally see why this scene would have needed tweaking, but I think it's perfect now.

When I first watched Obsession , I felt a chill down my spine when Bear called the number on the back of the One Wish Willow box. Then, I subsequently had so many questions about what was going on! When I talked to Barker about this scene, he revealed he was the one on the other side of the line.

What a fun cameo! I had no idea Barker was the voice , but it’s a fun little tidbit I’ll always think about when I watch that scene. He gave us some interesting insight about what’s going on with that phone call, too. I'm never forgetting Nikki's screams on the other line.

One more BTS detail I want to share has to do with what didn’t make it into the film. Obsession really goes hard in the paint on the movie rating scale, so I was curious if there was a scene the director had to remove because it went too far. The answer is, yes, there was one moment.

So, what was that “one thing”? During a Q&A (via Deadline ), Barker revealed it was the scene where Nikki kills Sarah by smashing her head into the steering wheel. Barker said there was originally “about six or seven more smashes." The MPA ratings board was going to give the movie a NC-17 rating because of it. At first, Barker wasn’t happy about making the change, but when he saw the movie with an audience (and heard their reactions), he realized the number they landed on was “the right number” to choose.

Avatar: The Last Airbender originally kicked off the franchise with Nickelodeon decades ago, and with it introduced animation fans to a whole new kind of world […]

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avatar: Seven Havens might be approachable for younger audiences and fans of all ages, but those behind the series don't really see it as just a show for kids. Avatar: The Last Airbender originally kicked off the franchise with Nickelodeon decades ago, and with it introduced animation fans to a whole new kind of world through its run. Then it was taken in an even darker direction with releases like The Legend of Korra and Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender in the years since . For Avatar: Seven Havens , it kind of sits in the middle.

Avatar: Seven Havens might star a very young set of twin Avatars for this new era of the franchise, and it might be designed in a different way than The Legend of Korra , but it takes on some intense subject matter that's especially seen withe final episodes of the debut season. As executive producer Sehaj Sethi explained in a Reddit AMA for the series, the team always intended to make it "accessible to a younger audience, but also be very interesting to older viewers."

"Personally, I think this show really isn’t a kids show," Sethi stated when asked about whether or not Avatar: Seven Havens was intended for audiences around Pavi and Nisha's age of 10-11. "The themes we cover are quite dark and mature. We always intended for this show to technically be accessible to a younger audience, but also be very interesting to older viewers ." Elaborating on this further, Sethi explained that they're not holding back on putting Pavi and Nisha through the wringer, "Even though Nisha and Pavi are children, we don’t hold back on making them face truly traumatic experiences."

Series producer Ethan Spaulding teased that Avatar: Seven Havens is going to get darker from here on out as well, "[T]he show definitely gets darker as the story progresses," but played coy as to whether or not it has a chance of getting as dark as The Legend of Korra did. Either way, this is something that has already been put in place with the final episodes of the first season as it has tackled xenophobia, isolationism, fear as a result of that and more. With Pavi exploring more Havens in the coming season , we're bound to see more of these intense topics.

Avatar: Seven Havens has been in development for the past few years before the first season finally premiered, and speaking to ComicBook, stars Aishu Devan (Nisha) and Saheli Khan (Pavi) revealed that they had been working on the show since they were 10-11 years old themselves. Noting that production on the third and fourth season had already begun, all they could tease was that there would be plenty of "character development" for the twins moving forward. So it seems like Pavi and Nisha are going to age alongside all of the events in the series.

It won't be too much longer before we see what's next as Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is already scheduled to kick off its run with Paramount+ beginning on May 21st next year. The new season will be 13 episodes long, and then followed by 13 more episodes with Season 3 releasing later in 2027. The series will then come to an end with Season 4 some time after, so how do you feel about Avatar: Seven Havens right now? Is it a kids show? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Obi-Wan Kenobi Simps Would Have Loved To Own This Piece Of Ewan McGregor's Star Wars History

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Hello there! Are you discussing the best ever Jedi in the Star Wars universe is? Of course, Anakin Skywalker is a good shout, considering he's the chosen one, and is also the protagonist of the prequel trilogy and The Clone Wars animated series. There's Yoda too, with his wisdom and unique lightsaber technique. And let's not forget Luke. However, the truth is that it's not even a debate. Obi-Wan Kenobi is the best Jedi Master of all time. Fans love him so much that someone paid $6,000 for his Padawan braid from 1999's Star Wars: Episode I - The Phantom Menace . Anyone who doubts his credentials should remember that he took down Darth Maul after watching him slay his master, made General Grievous flee in fear, and beat Anakin/Darth Vader twice. Even in his third canonical duel with Vader, Kenobi lets the Sith Lord strike him down.

The braid was worn by Ewan McGregor in The Phantom Menace , whose voice, mannerisms, and sheer sass went on to make him one of the fan favorite characters from the prequel trilogy, as well as The Clone Wars . The 17″ long braid is meant to signify that he is a Padawan under the tutelage of a Jedi Master, namely Qui-Gon Jinn. Unfortunately, Kenobi would soon have to give up the braid very quickly due to the death of Qui-Gon, and face the harsh reality of training his own Padawan. Of course, the fact that his Padawan was the Chosen One and a complete wildcard didn't make it easy. The braid is in decent shape overall, but features some adhesive residue from when it was stuck to McGregor's head, but that's an added bonus, as it may contain traces of the actor's real hair in it. You know… for those you care for such things.

While it may seem like just a bunch of long hair to some, Star Wars fans will know that it represents the origins of one of the franchise's most important characters. In fact, if it wasn't for Obi-Wan, Palpatine's plans for a Galactic Empire would have likely come to fruition much sooner, and there would be no one to steer Luke towards his destiny all those decades later. If you want to take the entire canon into consideration, he also orchestrated decisive victories against the Separatists during the Clone Wars. And to think he started off as a bright eyed Padawan with this very braid. He eventually went on to achieve great things, and even greater hair.

While this item is definitely an amazing collectible for fans and Obi-Wan stans, it presents a slight challenge when it comes to display. While you can mount Darth Vader's lightsaber on a display stand or a shelf, showing off Obi-Wan Kenobi's Padawan braid is a bit more complicated. You might have to create a custom case which displays the braid in a nicely laid out manner. Regardless of whether the new owner will display it or not, it's an amazing collectible, connected to arguably the greatest Jedi that has ever lived.

Who do you think is the greatest Jedi Master of all time? Let us know in the comments!

articles.content:
The hype surrounding the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI has reached a fevered pitch, with reviews for the game universally saying it’s living up to that hype. The GTA series has consistently been one of the most popular gaming franchises of all time, and one of the most successful entertainment franchises on Earth . It’s also one of the only monster franchises that hasn’t been adapted as a movie or a TV show.

Never mind who’s onstage at this year’s Kennedy Center Honors. Keep an eye on the banners.

Donald Trump ’s efforts to put his name on the performing arts institution continue to be thwarted by a federal court. But this year, while the Kennedy Center’s main building is closed for renovations — and still, after five months, remains shrouded by a tarp hiding the building’s original signage — the Dec. 7 honors ceremony is moving to Washington’s Capital One Arena, where the judge’s no-name-changing order may not apply. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Trump Says Federal Film Tax Credit Is Gaining Momentum Movies Mind the Gap: British Producer-Financier Phil Hunt Is Bringing Head Gear Stateside

“The injunction may only block Trump from affixing his name to the physical building that’s owned by the federal government,” says a source familiar with the Kennedy Center’s inner workings, noting that it remains “a very good question” as to whether there will be “Trump-Kennedy Center” branding at the Capital One event. After all, we know how much the president loves top billing.

If Trump’s name does end up on posters and programs, it’s unlikely the recipients will object too strenuously. This year’s crop of honorees — David Mamet, Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia and Barbara Mandrell — ranges from outspoken Trump admirers to, at least publicly, Trump agnostics. Also in normal times, honorees were traditionally announced in midsummer. But this year, like last, they came months later. articles.title: Boy George on His Controversial Israel Trip, Ed Sheeran and the Friends He Lost Along the Way
articles.summary: The Culture Club singer names the former collaborator who told him “Shame on you” and backs Robert Kraft’s decision to bar Macklemore from Gillette Stadium: “You can take your freedom of speech over there and do it on the street.”
articles.content:
Boy George wrote his new single, "We Will Dance Again," after visiting the Nova Exhibition in London, an immersive installation that commemorates the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on the Nova Music Festival that resulted in the deaths of 378 people and 44 people taken hostage.

He did it, he says, to send a message to his Jewish friends: "Not everybody hates you. You are loved."

The Culture Club frontman, 65, was not nearly prepared for the massive backlash that ensued, which spilled outside of social media into friendships that went back years. Among them was his collaborator Martyn Ware, the founder of New Wave bands like Human League and Heaven 17, who messaged him: "Shame on you." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Basque Cinema Expands Its (Rapidly) Growing Footprint in Tallinn TV 'Slow Horses' Actress Ruth Bradley to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive)

Undeterred, he recently visited Israel and played two sold-out shows at Tel Aviv's Menora Mivtachim Arena on Nov. 4 and 7. He also met with Israeli president Isaac Herzog and Nova survivors.

With his single now officially released and available on most streaming platforms, Boy George checked in with The Hollywood Reporter on a stop in Chicago.

He opened up about his Israel trip, explained why he used AI to make "We Will Dance Again" and revealed where he stands on the Ed Sheeran / Macklemore controversy that resulted in Sheeran's entire band walking off of his world tour.

What's a memory you cherish from the trip to Israel?

One of the sweetest things to me was people from London saying, "Oh, my aunt's in Israel, can she come and see you? And will you say hello?" And I met a few friends of mine's families that they haven't seen for years. And just meeting the Nova survivors, that was probably the highlight of the whole trip, because you suddenly understand why this journey started in the first place. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I saw the Nova exhibition in L.A. It's a very, very dark exhibit. When you played Israel, didn't some of the survivors come onstage with you?

Yeah. There was about 13 survivors and also people that lost family. So it was a real mix of people. I think it was really beautiful to let people be seen. And obviously, as a performer, you are uncomfortable because you don't want to hijack someone else's experience. You want to show it respect, but at the same time, going to Israel was a massive statement, and I had to be bold about it.

Somebody that reviewed my show said I should have snuck in quietly. I was like, "That wasn't an option." And sneaking in quietly right now is not helpful because nobody else is being quiet. So I don't think it's the time to be quiet. I think it's the time to be clear and to be loving. And I've made some mistakes in my communication online. There are people I shouldn't have bothered reacting to.

You've said you've lost friends over this. Is there anyone you'd name?

Martyn Ware, who was in Human League and Heaven 17. I've worked with Martyn. I did a version of "I Wanna Be Your Dog" with him, and we sung onstage together. He came out quite early and said, "Shame on you," and all of that. I just tweeted back, "You've lost that loving feeling. "

Most of them I don't want to name because I don't want them to have any more attention than they've already had from me.

You've said the music industry has been very one-sided on this. Do you find most people in the industry are anti-Israel? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I don't think they're anti-Israel. I just think they're not necessarily informed about history, and it's become quite trendy to shout certain things out. There's a lot of pressure to agree with everybody else. Your thought, my thought, are not the deciding factor on what happens in the Middle East. We've got nothing to do with it. We're not going to change it. So what we can do is, in our immediate surroundings, be more loving, be more open, be more kind, respectful, all of those things that you can do.

I was getting messages from friends of mine all over the world. Some people I didn't even know were Jewish. And I've had letters from people. So there is a lot of support out there, but it is scared of itself.

When I saw you speaking up for your Jewish friends on Ireland's Late Late Show in May , I knew you had something in your heart that needed expressing. I didn't realize to what extent it would end up expressing itself.

When I decided to make this record, I was sending a message to my friends to say, "Not everybody hates you. You are loved." And that's the point I tried to make when I was in Ireland, is that growing up during the punk period, one of my biggest allies was a man called Philip Sallon.

One of the first things he ever said to me was, "You look Irish." And I said, "I actually am." And he said, "I'm a Jew and a homosexual." And that was 1976. And when you're young and impressionable, you don't forget those moments. And Philip was a big reason why I got to know so many Jewish people because in London, this one knows that one, that one knows that one. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I can't sit here and say every single Jewish person I've ever met I've got on with. Of course I haven't. But Jewish people are characterful, they're kind, they're passionate, they're funny, they're bitchy. They've got all the qualities that I love.

You said you used AI to make "We Will Dance Again." What aspect of the song uses AI?

The music I wrote with an AI tool. The melody I [wrote], the words I [wrote] And the reason I used AI was because I didn't want somebody hanging over my shoulder saying, "Oh, you can't say that. Oh, that's too harsh." And that would've happened because I've had 40 years of that. Forty years of "That's too gay, that's too this, that's too that, that's not commercial."

I make a lot of music. I put out almost 200 tracks in the last two or three years. So I'm always writing. In respect to "We Will Dance Again," that line, that's a hook. You hear it straight away. As a writer, you go, "Got it. I got it. OK, there we go."

I saw a video where you were performing a concert and the music cut out and you kept singing a cappella . I couldn't tell whether it was intentional sabotage or a technical snafu. What happened?

I think it was a "technical snafu." I love that word. I don't think it was deliberate. There was a couple of moments when the mic went and I wasn't sure whether I'd pulled out the wire. And also the guitar went out in a really pivotal moment, but I kept my cool. We were in the round, so there was nowhere to hide. When you're in a proscenium situation, you can always dart off into a curtain for a minute, but in this instance, you couldn't really leave. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What it reminded me of is Ed Sheeran, who went onstage after his band walked out on him and did his show a cappella.

In the moment, you always have to remember that people have paid to see you and that you're there to perform. You can't get lost in something, but it can really distract your whole evening. I think it's really important to go, "No, no, no, I have to get through this."

Do you have anything else to say about Ed Sheeran in terms of that whole controversy regarding Macklemore being dropped from his tour?

Obviously, the stadium owner, Robert Kraft , I know that he's Jewish. He spent a long time fighting antisemitism, so he was never going to allow that to carry on where he worked, where he's an owner.

You have a choice who comes and sits at your dinner table, whether you're a billionaire or a housewife, you make a choice. And if you've cooked the meal and paid for the building, you do have a right as a person, as a Jewish person, to say, "No, you can take your freedom of speech over there and do it on the street."

I told my editor that "Do You Really Want to Hurt Me" is like a Jewish mother song.

articles.summary: With Basque filmmakers in the Tallinn Spotlight section and buzzy competition title 'Caballé,' the never-healthier regional production hub is reaching territories not yet conquered: "It opens different doors."
articles.content:
This year, Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) is letting Basque cinema bask — pun intended — in the spotlight.

Through dedicated investment over the last 10 years, the Basque film and TV output has never been stronger. The region has attracted productions from all over the world thanks to an alluring 60 percent tax rebate — increasing to 70 percent for projects shot in the Basque language, Euskara — allowing the area to lay claim to Catherine Zeta-Jones' Kill Jackie and Nanni Moretti's It Will Happen Tonight , among a slew of Spanish projects that catapulted the region to a record 45 Goya nominations earlier this year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'Slow Horses' Actress Ruth Bradley to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive) Movies 'In Starland': How Ray Panthaki, in His Directing Debut, Cast Clarence Maclin in His First Lead Role and Made a Very Personal Film Built on Meritocracy

This week, Tallinn's Spotlight section represents the booming Basque audiovisual in territory not yet conquered. "It opens different doors," begins Laura Lizuma, a Latvian producer based in San Sebastian who comes to the festival as part of the Basque delegation this year. "If the Basque country was in the spotlight in Argentina and Spain , that would be understandable — but the Basque industry is very small and when we think about global cinema… It's a great place to discover new possibilities of co-production because [when else] would a Basque producer come to Estonia or the Baltic states?"

Lizuma arrives in the Estonian capital as a producer on The River Woman , one of three Basque projects selected as part of the Tallinn Spotlight to receive development support. The feature film, directed by Tamara García Iglesias and co-written with Jon Bilbao, is described by Lizuma as "a rather unconventional western — one that takes the familiar codes of the genre and turns them around to tell a story from a woman's perspective." "I was interested in her contradictions," Ortega begins to The Hollywood Reporter about what drew her to the famed opera singer, depicted in the film by Begoña Alberdi. "Her strength and vulnerability, her doubts and insecurities, but also her determination to make her way in a world dominated by men."

Ortega describes the Basque contribution as "an essential part of bringing Caballé to the screen." This doesn't just refer to the production side of things, but also to the talent, commitment and "generosity" of those who worked on the film. I think she would have appreciated that spirit of collaboration."

She vouches for the work of the Basque crews and support from the region's government, saying that Bilbao's logistical strengths made the filming process "much easier." "Having a delegation in Tallinn creates opportunities to meet people, establish direct contacts and develop potential collaborations," says Cabero, who adds that a representative for the Etxepare Basque Institute, the organization leading the promotion of Basque culture internationally, will be talking in Tallinn about the tempting tax incentives. "I think all these elements help demonstrate just how much can be achieved in such a small territory," says Cabero.

The Basque shorts program, Kimuak, had one film — Raúl Barreras's Meanwhile, Then — premiere in the PÖFF Shorts section over the weekend. Six shorts from previous editions are set to screen through the rest of the festival as part of the Basque Spotlight. Interestingly enough, it's also Lizuma's appreciation for the Basque Country's sweeping landscapes that will help The River Woman achieve high-scale cinema at a lower cost. "With this project, in particular, the first idea is to shoot in the Basque Country because of the nature," says Lizuma. "We are planning to shoot between the Basque Country and Navarre, but this project is developed from the beginning to be an international co-production. Lizuma has lived in Spain for 10 years now and can measure in great depth the success of the concentrated backing of the Basque film and TV sector. And while Ortega's award hopeful filmed mostly in one of the region's busiest and most vibrant cities, what strikes her about Basque cinema is its ability to simultaneously straddle a particular place and culture while speaking to audiences far beyond it. "There isn’t just one Basque cinematic voice," she says, "there are many filmmakers with distinct sensibilities, and that diversity is one of its great strengths."

She touts the work of David Pérez Sañudo, who recently presented the brilliant Sacamantecas , Alauda Ruiz de Azúa with the five-time Goya Award-winning Los domingos , and Estibaliz Urresola's 20,000 Species of Bees , shortlisted for best international feature at the 2024 Oscars. This particularly personal testament is indicative of the kind of relationships the Basque audiovisual industry has so far managed to cultivate. Will Tallinn also succumb to the region's undeniable charm?

articles.title: One Piece's New Movie Could Change the Anime Forever
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation One Piece has been airing for more than 25 years, and over its long run, it has become a part of many fans' lives. However, it could change forever with a new One Piece movie releasing next year. What One Piece became known for was being the longest-running shonen anime, releasing new episodes every Sunday […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One Piece has been airing for more than 25 years, and over its long run, it has become a part of many fans' lives. However, it could change forever with a new One Piece movie releasing next year. What One Piece became known for was being the longest-running shonen anime, releasing new episodes every Sunday since 1999, with a few breaks here and there. However, that long-running legacy came to an end when, in 2025, it was announced that starting in 2026, the anime would embrace a 26-episode-per-year format, releasing in only two seasons. This brought an end to the legacy the anime had built over 26 years.

This year, fans got their first look at how this new anime format affected the series, and it is evident that the change will keep the anime on air for a longer time, as the pacing remains largely the same as it was under the old format. However, this year also brought new announcements from Toei Animation, revealing that the studio is working on two movies. One of them, One Piece Film: God Valley , is scheduled to release next year and will adapt events from the original source material, something the series has never done before. This signals a change that could transform the One Piece anime forever.

Up until now, every One Piece movie produced has featured an original story, something fans could easily skip since it was never aligned with the main storyline. This meant that if an anime movie failed to receive a theatrical release in certain regions for various reasons, it wasn't a problem. One of the main factors with anime movies is that they first release in Japan, while international fans have to wait at least a couple of months, if not longer, to watch them. This wouldn't normally be a problem, but with the new One Piece movie being canon and adapting a major narrative, it could be devastating for international fans who want to experience the movie as soon as it releases. This will certainly be a problem for major Western countries, as seen with Demon Slayer .

Even though Demon Slayer is a huge franchise, especially in the movie format, its latest movie took two months to receive an international release. Considering the upcoming One Piece movie will be a theatrical exclusive for some time, potentially for at least six months, fans who miss it in theaters for whatever reason could face a long wait before it becomes available on streaming platforms. Unlike anime episodes, which release weekly, this could create a significant delay. This essentially means that it could take even longer for One Piece to actually come to an end, something that some fans who want the franchise to last longer may consider a blessing in disguise.

Another impact One Piece 's new movie could have on the anime is that, if it becomes a huge success, which is certainly possible given its potential, newer arcs of the series could also be adapted into movies rather than episodes. This could follow the recent trend of popular franchises receiving theatrical anime releases, such as Haikyuu and Demon Slayer , particularly for their finales. Only time will tell how the final arc of the anime will be presented to fans, but it is clear that the wait for the franchise to end has already been extended. In many ways, the One Piece anime has already changed forever.

When it was announced that the anime would be following a 26-episode-per-year format , it became clear that the old One Piece anime had already come to an end, with a new, modern format being introduced to the franchise. With the new canon adaptation in movie form, the modernization of the anime franchise has become even more evident. Moreover, One Piece has already embraced the modern anime format more than most other series, all thanks to Netflix's ambitious project: a reboot of the anime. Netflix will release seven episodes adapting the first arc of the series, with all episodes dropping simultaneously.

This will serve as an entry point for new fans of the series going forward, offering a modernized way to experience the story without having to watch Toei Animation's adaptation, which consists of over 1,000 episodes. This could also encourage Toei Animation to change its strategy for the anime adaptation, potentially fully embracing the movie format for future arcs, with faster pacing and theatrical releases on the big screen. All these elements point toward the anime industry changing forever, and One Piece 's new movie format could mean longer waits for international fans to watch canon events, unless the franchise plans simultaneous international releases, a possibility that unfortunately seems unlikely.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Following a prominent leak this past week , Wizards of the Coast has officially announced that its next Secret Lair drop for Magic: The Gathering will be tied to the Dune franchise. To coincide with the upcoming release of Dune: Part Three , which hits theaters on December 18th, MTG will be collaborating with the acclaimed sci-fi series with an array of new cards. For those looking to get their hands on these new Dune x Secret Lair cards for themselves, you'll want to begin setting money aside right now.

Set to launch on November 30th at 12pm ET/9am PT, Wizards of the Coast will push live the "My Arrakis, My Superdrop" with three unique sets. The first group of cards, dubbed "Balance of Power", primarily includes Legendary Creature cards for Dune characters like Paul Atreides, Chani, and Princess Irulan. This drop will contain eight cards in total and will retail for $49.99, with its non-foil version costing $39.99.

The second drop is then dubbed "Deserts of Arrakis" and primarily hinges on Dune's iconic sandworms. These cards contain creatures like Shai-Hulud to go along with Legendary Artifacts like the Crysknife. Deserts of Arrakis will only contain six cards and will also retail for $49.99 and $39.99 (non-foil).

The last group of the bunch, simply called "Spice", is also the priciest of the bunch. These six cards include the likes of Water of Life, Pain Box, and Revel in Riches, the last of which is a wholly new card to MTG . The Spice set will go for $59.99 and will only be available to purchase in a foil format.

You can check out all of these cards in question that are part of the My Arrakis, My Superdrop release here:

For those who look to purchase all three of these Secret Lair x Dune drops, Wizards of the Coast will also include one special foil promo card. This card, which is dubbed Emperor’s Hutment as Reliquary Tower, will only be given to those who spend $149 as part of a single transaction. While the easiest way to reach this amount is by purchasing all of the individual drops in this Dune release, other Secret Lair drops that are available on the website should qualify for this promotion as well.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Vice City is alive, but not all of its seedy pleasures are up for grabs in Grand Theft Auto 6 . In fact, some fans might be surprised to hear that the franchise's well-known salacious activities are no longer on the menu. That's right, players will not be able to casually solicit prostitution in an interesting reversal of a mechanic that dates back to 2001's Grand Theft Auto III . But the reason is actually not all that surprising if you have any indication of the game's premise.

Rockstar Games actually addressed the absence of prostitution within the game highlighting the harm that it'd actually do to the story they're trying to tell. In a response to Shacknews , Rockstar Games stated the following:

" GTA VI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA VI , but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia’s story."

This feels obvious given the nature of the game's protagonists and their naturally intimate relationship. Rockstar Games has shared plenty of details in the past, noting that players can further the relationship between Jason and Lucia through various romantic means including dating, holding hands, dancing, and more. While the absence of such a mechanic may be a first for the series, at least in the past two decades, countless other GTA tropes still exist within the world of Grand Theft Auto 6 .

With the hype for Grand Theft Auto 6 at an all-time high given the imminent launch we're rapidly learning more about the game that is just mere hours away from a wide release. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will never receive a 60fps mode on current console hardware. Fans hoping for an eventual update may be disheartened by this news. Meanwhile, many are still wondering whether GTA Online will make its way to Rockstar's latest entry. Find out what Rockstar has said about a future multiplayer option . In other news, you may be wondering if a GTA movie will ever gain any traction. Recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick opened up about the possibility of a cinematic version of Grand Theft Auto coming to fruition .

With all that said, and knowing that GTA's more risqué pasttime is off-limits, what are the first activities or GTA traditions that you're excited to engage in with the launch of GTA 6 ? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Once upon a time, the Marvel Cinematic Universe was the most popular thing in pop culture. From 2008 to 2019, the first three Phases of the MCU were the blockbusters, taking Marvel Comics from a niche interest of the coolest people you know (comic fans are known for being much cooler than everyone else and I won't hear anything that says otherwise) to something that everyone you knew thought was the greatest piece of superhero fiction ever… even though most of them knew nothing about superheroes. When their favorite actors left the MCU, so did they, these "diehard" Marvel fans abandoning the franchise.

The Multiverse Saga has been something of a disappointment, partly because it just wasn't as good as what came before, partly because they had to switch directions on the set-up because of Jonathan Majors' crimes. Avengers: Doomsday is about to end the whole thing and the sad part is we've barely seen any cool multiversal Earths in the MCU. Marvel Comics is known for their awesome alternate Earths and these five should have been in the movies. Luckily, it's not too late so salvage the Marvel Cinematic Multiverse.

"Old Man Logan" was huge right away. Part of this is because it was a Wolverine story – anyone who thinks he isn't on Spider-Man's level (and above the MCU Trinity's as well) of popularity is wrong – and part of this was because it was the Civil War team of Mark Millar and Steve McNiven. The story took readers to an alternate universe where "Acts of Vegeance" – the villains attacking heroes they don't usually fight – succeeded, leading to the deaths of most of the heroes. Wolverine was mind-controlled into killing the X-Men, becoming a pacifist and moving to the Hulk Gang's territory after a trip to Japan with his wife.

The story was about Logan taking a bodyguard job for Hawkeye, taking readers across the Wastelands, the remainders of the United States under the control of the villains. "Old Man Logan" was just the first story that took readers there; since then, there have been numerous other stories set there. It's become a favorite of fans and it would be cool to see it on the big screen. I don't think the MCU should adapt "Old Man Logan" – it's not the kind of story they're good at – but they should bring in the Wastelands.

The Dark Ages came out in 2021. Marvel was trying to get one last story out of Tom Taylor before he signed his DC exclusive contract and the result was this book with Iban Coello. The Earth is attacked by Unmaker, leading the heroes and villains to team up to save reality. However, their solution to the threat of the cosmic titan ends up destroying nearly all technology on the Earth, leading to a dark new world of alliances, as the survivors scrape in the debris of civilization for the tools they'll need to see the next day. It wasn't massively popular – Taylor never had the following at Marvel that he did at DC and the House of Ideas didn't advertise the book very much – but it was pretty cool.

Dark Ages Earth would be an interesting MCU setting. One of the things about the MCU is that it followed the example of the first Ultimate Universe, meaning a lot of it was "grounded". Tech was a huge part of the setting, so seeing all of these characters we know and love trying to live without it would be awesome. Plus, the X-Men play a big role in it and since they're the next big MCU thing, this would have fit beautifully into the cinematic multiverse.

The X-Men are about to become the focus of the MCU. Sure, one day, we'll get reboots of the Avengers characters and they'll be popular again, but the MCU is about to become an X-Men world. The Multiverse Saga saw numerous mutants debut, with Deadpool/Wolverine concentrating on the mutant corners of the mutliverse. We got to see one of the coolest alternate Logans of all time in Weapon X, the Logan of the classic "Age of Apocalypse", during this sequence. However, all we got was a glimpse of him; we never got to actually see the Age, whether it be on the big screen or Disney+.

X-Men fans love "Age of Apocalypse" ; it was one of the most popular stories of the '90s, when the X-Men were huge (if your parents were '90s teens or babies, ask them about it; there's a good chance that they'll know about the story's existence, at the very least). I have no doubt that the MCU will bring it to screens eventually, but they honestly should have done it already. Deadpool/Wolverine had the chance to give us Wade talking smack about the Age and that would have been fantastic. Who knows, maybe we'll get lucky and it'll show up in Avengers: Doomsday or Avengers : Secret Wars .

Marvel Comics has lots of alternate futures, but most of them are honestly terrible. I don't mean that as a quality judgment, since Marvel does dark alternate future better than anyone (DC has some good ones, but it doesn't fit them nearly as well), but in that they're excellent at creating harrowing alternate Earths. What If… was the epicenter of this, but we did sometimes get some hopeful endings from those stories. What If… (Vol. 2) #105 was about the Spider-baby, who had just "died" at the end of the Clone Saga. This issue posited that she survived and ended up becoming Spider-Girl, from the team of Tom DeFalco and Ron Frenz. Fans loved Mayday Parker and soon, she got her own book.

This book would lead to the birth of MC2. This was the Marvel Universe of the future, with the children of various heroes taking up the mantles of their parents, following in the family business. MC2 was able to avoid cancellation numerous times, but it's since faded away almost completely. It was always kind of awesome (although very much grounded in late '90s Marvel, since that was what the future was being built off) and the best way for it to come back in the comics is for the MCU to do it. The MC2 would have been perfect for The Multiverse Saga and maybe if we're lucky, we'll still get to see it.

Earth X is an underrated Marvel gem , another example of Marvel's dark alternate future dominance. The genesis of this alternate Earth was actually DC. Kingdom Come from Mark Waid and Alex Ross was huge and Wizard Magazine asked Ross to Kingdom Come the Marvel Universe after that DC classic ended. This would lead to him teaming up with writer Jim Krueger and artist John Paul Leon for the 14-issue series Earth X . The book took place in a future where everyone on Earth gained superpowers after an accident with a vibranium-based power technology. However, the actual reason was bound up with the history of humanity and what really created us.

Earth X, Universe X , and Paradise X are, in my not-so humble opinion, a perfect representation of what makes the Marvel Universe so great. It's dark, yes, but there's also hope and love leading the way. It would be amazing to see it on the big screen and we still could. Alternate futures don't usually hold much truck with hope and would be cool to see our MCU favorites on this Earth.

What alternate Marvel Earths do you want to see in the MCU? Do you think Marvel Studios did a good job creating their multiverse? Sound off in the comments below.

articles.title: Does Georgia Still Want to Be the Hollywood of the South?
articles.summary: At a time when the fight for productions is fierce, new governor Keisha Lance Bottoms faces a major question - and challenge.
articles.content:
A few years ago, if you wanted to shoot a movie in Georgia, you’d better have made your reservations early.

The lack of an annual cap on credit payouts, the solid 30 percent rebate, the allowance of (some) above-the-line expenses, and the lower cost of housing compared with New York and California made it so that every inch of the state’s 21st century studio space and hotel inventory could get booked up.

MacGyver , Ozark , Stranger Things , The Resident and nearly every significant Marvel TV and film project were all among those calling Georgia home even when many of their stories were set elsewhere. And then there was Tyler Perry’s Fort McPherson studio and its 50,000 square feet of permanent sets, which opened in 2019 and housed numerous projects. The state’s film and TV growth was astronomical — over barely a dozen years beginning in 2010, studio square footage went from 45,000 all the way to 3 million.

But while Perry continues to book productions at his landmark location, Hollywood activity has thinned markedly in the Peach State since 2022. The Georgia Film Office reports that production spend has cratered from a peak of $4.4 billion in 2022 to $2.3 billion in 2025 — hardly peanuts ( Will Trent , The Rock’s Lizard Music and Judd Apatow’s The Comeback King have been among recent shoots) but a major fall. Total productions saw a similar drop, from 412 to 245.

And the numbers continue to sink. Industry tracker ProdPro says that Georgia saw about $1.56 billion in film and TV production spend in the 12 months ending in September, down 15 percent from $1.84 billion in the prior 12-month period.

There have been other worrisome developments. Lee Thomas, longtime head of the Georgia Film Office and the major force behind the surge, announced her retirement this summer. Her replacement has not been named. And then in early November, another blow: James Gunn, who famously loved Georgia and brought DC projects like Peacemaker and Superman to the sprawling Trillith Studios in Fayetteville, was ousted as head of the superhero division under new Skydance ownership.

Gunn’s love affair with Georgia runs deep; he shot the first two Guardians of the Galaxy movies for Marvel and even owned a home there. The director's big-budget Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow alone, which shot in the state this summer, gave Georgia its best production spend quarter for new shoots since early 2024, ProdPro notes. But his successor, Jeremy Latcham, and Latcham’s boss, David Ellison, could shop for preferred alternatives with less allegiance to the past.

Of course, there’s an overall decline in streamer and studio projects in the post-strike and -COVID era. And there have been bright spots even in Georgia, such as reeling in American Idol from Los Angeles to shoot its upcoming season in the state. But overall the news has been dark.

One big culprit of the Georgia drop? Generous tax credits overseas. A prominent TV producer says the location conversation with studios these days always starts with Budapest, then moves to Ireland before going to England. Marvel itself largely decamped for the U.K. in 2024. That puts Georgia in a tough spot.

This could change if a federal tax credit can gain momentum and pass in the new congressional session. But such a passage is far from guaranteed, and it still might not induce projects to come home. And New York is proving a formidable American rival to Georgia, seeing gains in many key metrics, with plenty of studio space being built in New Jersey to augment the effort.

Georgia’s lame-duck Republican governor and legislature are unlikely to follow through on longtime threats to reduce the credit before leaving office next month. But whether a new Democratic state house and new Democratic Gov. Keisha Lance Bottoms can or will reenergize the business remains an open question. One question: the new film commissioner could work under Pat Wilson, the state’s longtime commissioner of economic development — or Bottoms could find someone to replace Wilson. (Thomas will do some contract work in the meantime.)

A Georgia unraveling would spell more than an employment loss. Georgia crews tend to be more diverse than those in New York and Los Angeles, in particular with many Black women occupying positions they don’t hold in other places. And when the new soap opera Beyond the Gates won the Daytime Emmy for lighting direction in October, the winners were both Black men, a rarity in the category.

One encouraging sign for Georgia crews and the state’s Hollywood allies: Perry’s place in the Lance Bottoms administration. He was named to her transition team right after the election. But she has downplayed what that meant. “I think what people miss,” she told the popular morning program Yung Joc & The Streetz Morning Takeover when a host asked about the Perry appointment, “is that these are just co-chairs … we’ll probably have 100 more.” Lance Bottoms could have other priorities for tax money than putting it in producers’ pockets; the state recently ranked 49th in health care in one prominent annual study.

During his successful reelection bid, Democratic senator Jon Ossoff faced criticism from opponent Mike Collins that he was more concerned with Hollywood, California than [the small town of] Hollywood, Georgia, a criticism Lance Bottoms could be sensitive to as well.

And Perry himself is actually about to move to Puerto Rico to be closer to his son. He says activity at his studio will continue unabated, but what this all means for him and his Georgia advocacy remains to be seen. On the red carpet for his Tyler Perry’s The Gospel of Christmas recently he didn’t seem especially eager to talk about the credit. Asked about its future, he told THR , "Well as great as that's been [and it] has been amazing, for me, my focus is being pro-Georgia, and Keisha is pro-Georgia. So I want to make sure that businesses, people are taken care of."

The state's Hollywood advocates could take comfort in at least one fact: AI hasn’t cut into physical production in Georgia — yet.

This story appeared in the Nov. 12 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Click here to subscribe.
