articles.title: I Love Living In A World Where Brad Pitt And George Clooney Are Still Trolling Each Other After Decades
articles.summary: Never change, fellas. Never change.
articles.content:
There are so many A+ celebrity bromances, from Matt Damon and Ben Affleck to Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman . Of course, when talking about such male friendships, Brad Pitt and George Clooney have to be mentioned as well. The two Oscar winners have been friends for years, and a hallmark of the relationship is that the two enjoy taking playful shots at each other. That recently continued during some red carpet interviews, and I’m so glad this trolling between the two prank war participants is still going strong.

Spoken like two men who have a friendly rivalry of sorts, and this dynamic goes back quite a while. It was especially present when the pair worked together on the Ocean’s Trilogy, which began back in 2001. Since then, the two have kept their relationship playful, which has led to some great moments. Even earlier this year, Pitt – while promoting his canine-centric movie, Heart of the Beast – mused that a dog could’ve replaced Clooney in Ocean’s Eleven . That’s a great jab but, still, I love Clooney’s take on being able to outdance Pitt:

Talk about shots fired! Of course, it’s not at all surprising that the F1 star wouldn’t let that humorous critique go unanswered:

Of course, the self-deprecating actor also clarified that he couldn’t say with certainty that he’d outdo Clooney. His point was that he doesn’t necessarily “take pride in [his] dancing.” Of course, while Pitt and Clooney may take pleasure in skewering each other from time to time, they do have a genuine friendship and seem to really enjoy being around each other. That playful dynamic was apparently present when they worked on their most recent movie together.

articles.title: Miss Konosuba? You Need to Watch Crunchyroll's Funniest Fall Anime
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of P.A. Works If you're missing Konosuba: God's Blessing on this Wonderful World right now, there's a new anime now streaming with Crunchyroll this Fall that you really should give a chance. Konosuba has become a standout anime franchise because of the parodical take on Isekai stories. Featuring a group of would-be losers who band together to succeed, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you're missing Konosuba: God's Blessing on this Wonderful World right now, there's a new anime now streaming with Crunchyroll this Fall that you really should give a chance. Konosuba has become a standout anime franchise because of the parodical take on Isekai stories . Featuring a group of would-be losers who band together to succeed, it's basically like watching a team of gremlins failing upwards through their misadventures. The anime adaptation for Asa Rokushima's The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life perfectly taps into that same energy.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life may not be an Isekai anime series like Konosuba , but the two share a core that feels incredibly familiar. Both anime offer a group of individuals who often devolve into bouts of wild emotional states that alter their character designs , both groups are put into dangerous situations that are taken with various levels of seriousness, and both series are just having a lot of fun with how they progress through their story. It just scratches that same itch.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is set in a traditional fantasy world ( with teases of something else going on under the surface ) and falls in line with the power-fantasy stories seen in other offerings. Rein is an enchanter who can invest skill points into weapons and armor, but is soon kicked out of his party because he's seen as unnecessary. Only to then take back all of the points he's given out thus far and make his paltry clothes and weapons (which are sometimes just pebbles) stronger than anything else.

While it starts out with the same kind of hook that's usually seen with stories where the main character is kicked out of their party (only to be revealed to be secretly strong), it takes a much floatier route to how it gets to certain points. Rein is naive and a bit of a dullard, but takes his adventures seriously now that he's on his own. And in comparison to Konosuba, he's a much more capable person than Kazuma. It's the same for his party that slowly forms with additions like Lily (an S-Rank adventurer who was a shut-in for two years) and Margaret (who originally wants to kill Lily). The levels just keep building on from there.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life isn't as wacky as Konosuba when it comes to the nature of its stories, and that's ultimately what makes it even more compelling. Because while Rein, Lily and Margaret are seen having fun in almost a trolling kind of way with their adventures, there is a great deal of risk involved with the episodes seen thus far. There's no potential of revivals like Kazuma's, and thus it keeps the group from turning into full Looney Tunes characters like its counterpart.

The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is a lot like Konosuba in terms of the tone of its comedy and wacky character choices, but it most comes through in the production. While it's not as outwardly wacky and fluid as its counterpart, this series has a lot of effort in punctuating the wild scenes with a fun variety in the way it chooses to bring certain scenes to life. Action scenes will move with a cool fluidity then will be countered by the stuff faces of its cast to land the joke.

The series is directed by Shu Honma for P.A. Works, the studio behind anime such as Shirobako, Buddy Daddies, Skip and Loafer and more, and all of that expertise and personality is fueling the series. It leads to a perfect blend of cool action scenes with the hilarious comedy, and often results in an experience that's rarely seen elsewhere. But with so many new series now airing as part of the Fall 2026 anime schedule , this one has likely fallen through the cracks of your watching schedule.

Konosuba: God's Blessing on this Wonderful World is now in the works on Season 4 of the anime , but has yet to reveal a release date or window as of this time. With no clear indication of just how long the wait for its return is going to be, The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is a good way to scratch that itch for now in the meantime. You can find it now streaming on Crunchyroll with both Japanese and English language audio.

Have you checked out The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life this Fall? If so, what do you think of it so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.content:
Before Gordon Ramsay , culinary television was calm.

articles.title: Screen Gems Lays Off Staff as New Leader Comes In (Exclusive)
articles.summary: In October, Sony Pictures hired veteran YouTube executive Fede Goldenberg to lead the division and change its direction.
articles.content: Screen Gems has cleaned house, laying off a majority of its staff as the Sony division enters a new era under incoming head, former YouTube executive Fede Goldenberg. The division, which specializing in genre movies such as Resident Evil and Underworld and comedies such as Easy A , has let go of senior vp Nathan Samdalh, vp Ellie Walker, and creative exec Peyton Collins, among others, sources tell The Hollywood Reporter. Goldenberg made the cuts and is expected to bring in a new team as he takes Screen Gems in a new direction. The exec was hired in early October and is bringing in a decidedly 2026 focus to the label. Under the new creative strategy, the film label is expanding its longstanding focus on traditional genre films to include theatrical projects from the next generation of so called “digital-native storytellers,” meaning filmmakers who are making names — and gaining followers — in the digital content space a la Curry Barker of Obsession fame and Backrooms filmmaker Kane Parsons. Ashley Brucks, who had been running the label as president since 2023, transitioned to a producing role. Samdahl is the former Paramount executive who was instrumental in making the horror hit Smile (and was infamously let go from the studio before the movie became a surprise hit). He also acted as a creative exec at Walter Hamada’s production banner 18hz Productions. He joined Screen Gems in October 2025. Walker was also a former Paramount exec. She joined the Sony division in 2024. Collins was hired in 2024 after working previously at Jeff Robinov’s Studio 8.

articles.title: One Of Shonda Rhimes’ Best Shows Is Leaving Netflix (And So Is One Of My Favorite TV Couples)
articles.summary: Another goodbye for this couple is coming.
articles.content:
Over the years, Shonda Rhimes has been taking over television with dramas and romances that people can’t get enough of. Thanks to streaming, fans are able to rewatch and discover her projects. Scandal , for instance, is arguably one of Rhimes’ best shows, even eight years after its final season aired . Unfortunately, those streaming it with a Netflix subscription will soon have to say goodbye, meaning I have to say goodbye to one of my favorite TV couples, too.

For the second time since initially being added to Netflix back in 2014, Scandal is set to leave the streaming giant in December. This comes less than two years after the political drama rejoined Netflix in June 2025, five years after it originally left. Fans will have until December 17 to watch all seven seasons, and it’s unknown if Scandal will be added to Netflix again.

The reason for Scandal ’s departure from Netflix likely has to do with the licensing agreement with the streamer expiring. However, it’s unknown if another deal will be made. It’s definitely disappointing, considering Scandal was one of the best shows on television , and soon, a lot of people won’t be able to watch it. Luckily, Netflix is not the only place to stream Scandal .

I’m not one to wish for the downfall of a couple and root for an affair, but when it comes to Scandal , it’s kind of hard not to. Kerry Washington ’s Olivia Pope and Tony Goldwyn’s President Fitzgerald “Fitz” Thomas Grant III were the couple on Scandal . They had a tumultuous relationship as they denied feelings for one another pretty early on, since Olivia had worked on Fitz’s campaign and was the White House Director of Communications. Not to mention the fact that Fitz was married to Melody “Mellie” Margaret Grant (Bellamy Young). He later divorced her, and she was thriving without him, so it definitely all worked out in the end.
